_comment: Least-privilege policy for the PROXY when it runs under a dedicated IAM role (e.g. on EC2/ECS/Fargate) rather than a developer's local AWS credentials. Today the proxy runs locally under your own creds, so this file is NOT applied by setup_iam.sh — it documents the exact grant to attach when you move the proxy to a hosted role. The ONE privilege here is read access to the env-var encryption master key. That secret lives OUTSIDE the microvm/* prefix precisely so the VM exec role cannot read it; the proxy is the only component that seals/unseals env var values, so it is the only principal that needs this. A hosted proxy will ALSO need the permissions it currently inherits from local admin creds (lambda-microvms control plane, S3 artifacts, rds-data on the cluster, secretsmanager on microvm/*, bedrock, etc.) — add those alongside this statement; they are intentionally out of scope for this file, which covers only the new master-key grant.
